subject: MSA redlines: OSS indemnity and liability cap carve-outs

Subject: Nimble AI redlines - MSA (Liability / OSS)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are Nimble's redlines to your standard MSA. The key open items for us are:
- Limitation of liability: a mutual cap tied to fees for the prior 12 months plus carve-outs for willful misconduct and IP infringement.
- Consequential damages: we still want a narrow exception for data exfiltration losses tied to breach of security obligations.
- OSS/model licensing: we need an explicit indemnity for claims arising from licensed open-source components and model licensing constraints; pass-through to sub-suppliers is acceptable but must be uncapped for IP claims.

I've attached the redlined PDF (redlined_msa_20250910.pdf). Please confirm your legal's availability this week to discuss.

Best,
Sofia Martinez

Team / Sofia — reviewed the redlines and drafted alternative language attached (vendor_os_clause_draft.docx). High-level positions below: 

1) Overall cap: we can accept a mutual cap tied to aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months, with a separate carve-out for willful misconduct and gross negligence.

2) Consequential damages: Redwood's standard position is to exclude consequential damages broadly; however, we can accept a narrow exception for direct losses from proven data breach if caused by Redwood's failure to adhere to security obligations, subject to a sub-cap (e.g., 2x annual fees).

3) OSS / model licensing: we are uncomfortable with uncapped pass-through indemnity. Proposed compromise: 
   - Redwood will indemnify for third-party IP claims to the extent caused by Redwood's modification or distribution of OSS components or model artifacts provided by Redwood.
   - For OSS used by customer in their environment or provided by third parties, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify and cooperate but will not accept unconstrained pass-through liability.
   - Pass-through indemnity for subcontractors: limited to the indemnity Redwood actually receives from that subcontractor (no back-to-back uncapped liability).

4) Practical ask: if Nimble needs broader OSS pass-through (uncapped), we need commercial protection (higher cap or insurance) or an exception approved by leadership.

Please review the attached draft. If Nimble's counsel can highlight the specific legal basis for uncapped pass-through we can escalate.

— Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Nimble AI redlines - MSA (Liability / OSS)

Dev / Marissa — thanks for the quick review. From Nimble's perspective: 

- The concern with your proposed limitation is that our use of open models and third-party OSS in the pipeline exposes us to copyright and license-compliance claims that historically require pass-through relief. Several recent incidents in our industry forced customers to seek indemnity and direct recovery from vendors.

- We are not asking for an uncapped open-ended guarantee for all upstream code — rather, for an exception to the cap specific to third-party IP infringement claims that arise directly from licensed OSS distributed as part of the model package Redwood provides. That exception should not be limited by Redwood's subcontracts because Nimble relies on Redwood's supply chain.

If Redwood requires insurance or higher caps to accept that narrow carve-out, we can discuss cost-sharing. We'd prefer to avoid leadership escalations but can bring this up internally if needed. Please provide concrete redline language we can accept or mark up.

Sofia Martinez (on behalf of Nimble AI Legal)
sofia.martinez@nimbleai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimble AI redlines - MSA (Liability / OSS)

Sofia — thanks, constructive framing. Proposal from Redwood side to avoid escalation: 

1) Liability cap: mutual cap equal to total fees paid in prior 12 months. Carve-outs: (a) willful misconduct; (b) proven IP infringement claims arising from code or model artifacts provided directly by Redwood.

2) OSS / model IP carve-out (proposed redline snippet):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor's liability for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement arising from software or model artifacts that Vendor (a) packaged, distributed, or delivered to Customer as part of the Service, and (b) represented as being under a license that permits such use, shall not be subject to the liability cap set forth above. Such indemnity shall be limited to direct damages and reasonable defense costs and shall exclude consequential, incidental, or punitive damages."

3) Pass-through to subcontractors: Redwood will flow-through any indemnity it receives from its suppliers but will not accept greater liability than Redwood itself has accepted from such suppliers unless otherwise agreed in writing.

4) Consequential damages: continue general exclusion; include a narrow exception for direct losses from a documented data breach caused by Redwood's failure to comply with the Security Addendum, subject to a sub-limit of 2x the prior 12 months' fees.

If Nimble accepts the above language (modulo minor edits), we will produce an updated MSA and Order Form with the commercial cap reflected. Rachel — can you confirm the 2x sub-limit is acceptable financially or whether we should propose insurance instead?

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

Best,
Marissa
